page: Microsoft Azure EC48ads_v5 is an enterprise-grade, memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It utilizes the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 48 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory is scaled to 384.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio to accommodate data-heavy footprints. The instance bundles 1,933 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage, while containing zero discrete GPUs and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying AMD processor incorporates a cache layout of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction support includes AVX vector processing, FMA, BMI2, and cryptographic accelerations such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions. In standardized benchmarking, the platform demonstrates middle-tier baseline performance, delivering a stress-ng single-core score of 2333.15 and a multi-core score of 55471.64. In caching operations, the instance achieved a throughput of 44.78 million operations per second on redis SET benchmarks.

From an infrastructure perspective, the EC48ads_v5 balances compute capacity against substantial memory density. The integrated 1,933 GB local solid-state drive offers direct, low-latency temporary storage without the operational overhead of attaching secondary external block volumes. Because memory capacity is prioritized at 8 GB per vCPU, it functions cost-efficiently for memory-constrained workloads. However, workloads requiring specialized vector acceleration or extreme single-threaded compute will face architectural limitations due to standard instruction support and average per-core benchmark metrics.

The hardware profile makes the EC48ads_v5 well configured for memory-intensive workloads that require rapid local scratch caching. Key suitable deployments include in-memory databases like Redis, enterprise relational database systems, real-time analytics engines, distributed caching nodes, and high-throughput data transformation pipelines.
